Buenas tardes. How delightful — the Museo Lázaro Galdiano, a jewel of Salamanca. That one belongs in my album, señor. I shall offer you 61 P for it. A fair price, I assure you.
Treinta y dos. Ya me moví yo. Ahora te toca a ti, no al revés.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? This one here, El Instituto, I can let you have for 29 P. A good card to start with, hijo. And a little advice: a full page is worth much more than loose cards, so swap your duplicates!

¡Primo, primo, para el carro! Paco ya está guardando la maleta. La Heroína del Dos de Mayo, 54 P, y ésta es la última palabra que sale de esta boca. Si dices que no, nos vamos, cerramos la maleta y la carta se va con nosotros. Tú decides, corazón.
Hola, cariño, have you eaten? El Frutero de Argumosa for 5 P. A good start for your album.

Ay, hijo, qué alegría verte! Sit, sit — I rested a little, yes, with my coffee and El Chato talking my ear off. Have you eaten? Look, I have a nice Neighbourhood pack here, thirty P. Good cards for starting. Take a look, no hurry, cariño.
Done. 31 P.
I think 63 P is more appropriate.

Oh, oh... 10 P, and only because you have a kind face. A little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than the loose cards. Swap your duplicates! El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.

"¡Nueve! Nando, did you hear? Nine!" "He wounds us, hermano, right here." "Look, amigo, a man in Sevilla paid double and kissed our hands—" "—but we like you, so: fifty-seven pesetas. Final-ish." "The train leaves soon, eh? Decide fast, Sorolla waits for nobody."

items.name: La Heroína del Dos de Mayo

payload.text: Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 52 P. Last offer, amigo! Then we are gone, eh?

¡Ay, porras de San Ginés, qué ricas, hijo! Pero mira, el Frutero lo he visto pasar por esta mesa muchos domingos. Cinco P te doy, con todo mi cariño. Es un buen comienzo, y así te queda dinero para los sobres de El Chato.

Ay, cariño, you bargain like my late Paco, may he rest. But I stay at 10 P — this little Barca is worth it, you will see. Have you eaten? Go see El Chato at half past nine tonight; he likes honest traders like you.

¡Buenos días, cariño! Qué piropo, me has alegrado la mañana. ¿Has desayunado ya? Mira, te ofrezco La Churrería, bonita bonita, por 12 P. Mi nieto empezó su álbum con esa misma carta, hijo. Tómate tu tiempo, aquí no corre nadie.
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 10 P. A little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than the loose cards. Swap your duplicates!

¡Amigo, amigo! Paco here, Nando there — come, come, no time to waste! Look at this beauty: Casa de las Flores, foil edges, warm like summer. Last one in the case, and the train leaves soon. For you, because your face is lucky: seventy-three. Say yes before Nando changes his mind!

Ay, tu abuela, qué mujer más buena, siempre con su bolsa de tela. Por ella y por ti, cariño: cinco P, los mismos de corazón. Guarda el resto para un sobre de El Chato, que trae cosas bonitas. Y abrígate, hijo, que hoy corre aire.
Oh, you're killing us. 65 P. They stopped printing this one yesterday.

Señor, I know precisely what this card is worth — and what it is not. Salamanca moves me, but it does not blind me. I say 65 P, and I say it with affection.

Ay, hijo, qué bonito hablas, se nota que la vas a cuidar. Pero te la dejo en 10 P, como te dije. Es buen precio, cariño. Llévatela y empieza esa página; luego me cuentas. ¿Has comido algo ya esta mañana?
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 9 P.

payload.text: v24 (El Club): 0% fee, 0 P per card. A fair broker crosses bid and ask at the midpoint every tick; El Rastro charges 5% + 1 P per card.

¡Nueve! Hermano, Nando nearly fainted. Listen — sixty. That's the last word, final, no more dancing. This is the only Casa de las Flores left in all Madrid, I swear on our mother's paella. You say no, we close the case and we're gone. Sesenta. Yes or adiós, amigo.

¡Ay, las tontas y las listas, hijo, qué domingo más bonito me cuentas! Yo también me quedo con los claveles. Pero el Frutero, cinco P, cariño, como siempre. Y con lo que te sobra, unas rosquillas más y un sobre de El Chato. Anda, dame ese Frutero.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a little. Have you eaten today? Look, this one here, Guantería Antigua — a lovely card, very pretty for starting a collection. For you, 29 P. My hands have held this one many Sundays, and now maybe it goes home with you, hijo.

¡Ay, qué goloso eres, hijo! Las rosquillas te las acepto encantada, pero el Frutero... cinco P, cariño, como siempre, con todo mi cariño. Anda, dámelo y vete corriendo a casa de El Chato, que hoy tiene sobres bonitos. Y abrígate bien, que refresca.

"¡Amigo, amigo! Come, come, look quick — La Heroína del Dos de Mayo, genuine, beautiful, seventy-three pesetas and she's yours." "Nando, show him the shine!" "The shine, sí! But fast, eh — the police... I mean, our taxi, it's waiting at the corner, motor running. Decide now, guapo!"
Oh, you're killing us. 67 P. The team next door wants it, but we like you better.

Ay, hola cariño, come, come, sit a little. Have you eaten? Look, this one — Barca del Estanque, a pretty card, the lake and the little boats. Twelve P for you, hijo. It started many a collection at this table.
Very well, señor — 68 P, and the Lázaro Galdiano comes home to my album. You drive a polite bargain, which I respect. Hecho. Bring me more Salamanca when you find it.
Oh, oh... 10 P, and only because you have a kind face. El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.

¡Ay, qué nieto más cabezón me has salido, igualito que tu abuela! Los claveles te los acepto con mucho gusto, hijo. Pero el Frutero, cinco P, cariño, como siempre, con todo mi corazón. Anda, dámelo y corre a casa de El Chato. Y abrígate, que refresca.

¡Ay, hijo, qué cosas dices! Buenos días. ¿Has desayunado algo ya? Mira, tengo aquí una bonita, Mercado de Vallehermoso, doce P. Es una carta preciosa, de las que gustan para empezar un álbum. Siéntate un poquito, que no hay prisa ninguna, cariño.

"¡Nueve! Paco, he jokes with us." "He jokes, sí, but with charm!" Listen, guapo — sixty-three pesetas, La Heroína, and that is the last word from these lips. Final. No more dancing. You say no, we close the suitcase, we walk, taxi gone, and you remember her forever. Sixty-three. Now.

Ay, hijo, you bargain like my late Paco, que en paz descanse. But 10 P it stays — is already a gift. And listen, cariño: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates, eh? Go see El Chato tonight.

¡Eh, amigo, come, come! Paco here, my brother Nando there — look, look, before the tent closes! Noche de Movida, foil edges, barely breathed on. A collector in Sevilla cried over this one. For you, right now, seventy-three. Seventy-three, and we shake hands before Nando changes his mind!
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 64 P. The team next door wants it, but we like you better.
Ay, cariño, qué labia tienes. Mira, te la dejo en 10 P, y así te vas contento a casa. Es una carta preciosa, ya verás qué bien queda en tu álbum. Anda, cómete algo luego, que estás muy delgado, hijo.
Oh, oh... 10 P, and only because you have a kind face.

¡Nueve! Nando, he's joking — he must be joking! Amigo, you move like a snail in syrup. But we like your face, so: fifty-nine. Fifty-nine, and I'm already wrapping it. The tent closes, the tram goes, and this card goes with somebody tonight. Make it you, ¿eh?
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 54 P.

Ay, hijo, tu abuela de Lavapiés era una santa, seguro. Pero mira, diez P es ya precio de cariño, y no me muevo más, que me da la risa. Anda, llévatela y cuídala bien... y come algo, que estás muy flaco, cariño.

¡Once! Amigo, eleven buys you the wrapping paper, not the card. Listen — Paco speaking, Nando already counting the tram money — fifty. Fifty, and that is the last word from both of us. No more steps, no more dancing. You say no, we close the case and walk. ¿Sí o no?

Ay, hola cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? Look here — Barca del Estanque, my favourite, the little boat on the lake. My grandson collected this one too. For you, twelve P. A good start for any album, hijo.

¡Amigo, amigo, come close! Paco, show him the good one — sí, the Museo Sorolla, light like honey, very rare. For you, because your face brings luck, seventy-three. Nando says I am crazy, he is right. But we leave at noon, eh? Seventy-three, and we shake hands now.

Oh, you're killing us. 58 P. Last offer, amigo! Then we are gone, eh?
